docs.explain: SUMIF answers one question; most real totals ask two. SUMIFS takes the range to add first — which is the opposite order to SUMIF, and the reason people who know SUMIF get it wrong — then any number of range/condition pairs. In this drill the sum range is C2:C6, the region column must say North, and the rep column must say Ada, which leaves rows 2 and 6 and answers 720. The second screen swaps one pair for a comparison: the status must be Shipped and the amount must be over 200, so the 180 order is shipped but excluded and the answer is 620. Conditions are text or comparisons in quotes, and the wildcard characters work inside them. All the criteria ranges must be the same shape as the sum range, or rows start drifting against each other and the total is quietly wrong. When a condition needs an OR rather than an AND, SUMIFS cannot express it in one call: add two SUMIFS calls together instead of trying to bend one.

errors.text: The sum range holds text where a number was expected.
A condition or an argument divides by zero before the total is reached.
The function was typed as SUMIF, which takes different arguments and a different order.
